news.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observin
paras: In 1676 Denmark’s astronomer Ole Rømer studied Io, the moon that orbits Jupiter. He wanted to use Io’s regular visits as a cosmic clock. Each time Io vanished behind Jupiter, Rømer timed the moment it reappeared. His timing was off by about eleven minutes, depending on Earth's distance.
Rømer realised light moves at a finite speed, not instantly, because signals lagged. He calculated the delay to find light’s speed. His calculation of the delay gave the speed of light.

news.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Resistance is futile when it comes to the 'Next Generation' crew's greatest
paras: How cyber-zombies and the "birth of 'Star Trek'" gave Jean-Luc Picard one of his finest hours. "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command".

But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch.

sport.title: Coco Gauff admits the main reason why she is happy to be ranked above Jessica Pegula for a fourth year in a ro
paras: Coco Gauff has ended the season as the American WTA number one player for a fourth successive year. Gauff has had a mixed 2026 season , having failed to reach a Grand Slam final this year, but won her fourth WTA 1000 title at the Cincinnati Open .

The two-time Grand Slam champion played her most recent tournament at the WTA Finals , where Gauff was eliminated at the round-robin stage. Despite this, Gauff is still the American number one ahead of Jessica Pegula for a fourth consecutive year, as she leads her compatriot by just three ranking points.

sport.title: “It’s a mixed review”: Shelton sees plenty to improve after the best season of his career
paras: Beaten by Carlos Alcaraz in the ATP Finals semi-finals in Turin on Saturday, Ben Shelton weighed up a year with four titles, a first Grand Slam final and a career-high No. The American says his level has “improved dramatically”, but refuses to be cast as the third man behind Sinner and Alcaraz.

Ben Shelton is not giving his season full marks. “It’s a mixed review,” the American said on Saturday in Turin, after his 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) defeat to Carlos Alcaraz in the ATP Finals semi-finals, even though 2026 has been the best year of his career.

sport.title: “Be brave”: how Shelton’s plan worked for a set, until Alcaraz turned up the heat
paras: Ben Shelton followed his team’s advice to go for his chances and took the first set, before Carlos Alcaraz shouted his way out of a tense start and took over. The two men explained how their ATP Finals semi-final in Turin turned on Saturday.

Shelton For a set, Ben Shelton ’s plan worked. Then Carlos Alcaraz found a way back, and won the points that decided their ATP Finals semi-final 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) on Saturday in Turin, two weeks after beating the American in the Paris Masters final . Afterwards, both men talked about serving and about errors at the wrong moments, but even more about a clash of wills, a contest in which Alcaraz proved the stronger.

sport.title: Carlos Alcaraz admits why he was ‘frustrated’ during his match vs Ben Shelton in the semi-finals of the ATP Fi
paras: Carlos Alcaraz was pushed to his limits today, but managed to come from behind to beat Ben Shelton and reach a second successive ATP Finals final earlier today. The American came flying out of the blocks, breaking early and finishing off a near-perfect set to establish a well-deserved lead.

However, the seven-time Grand Slam champion was never going to vanish without a fight, and fight back he did, needing just a single break to win the second set, and claiming the crucial third on a match tiebreak. Speaking whilst still on court with Tennis Channel, Carlos Alcaraz unsurprisingly cut an upbeat figure.

sport.title: Jannik Sinner told he won’t be able to copy Novak Djokovic’s ‘miraculous’ injury comeback if he has knee surge
paras: Jannik Sinner has been absent from the tennis tour for four months now, ever since he beat Alexander Zverev to lift the Wimbledon title. Ironically, it is the German who has since taken advantage of this subsequent power vacuum, winning a second Grand Slam title whilst also ascending to world number one.

At the beginning, it felt like the Italian’s decision to withdraw from Canada, and later Cincinnati, was merely precautionary. However, it’s since become clear that something far more sinister was at play, with that same knee injury now persisting deep into November.

sport.title: Ben Shelton Shuts Down 2026 Season With Mixed Feelings
paras: Ben Shelton admits there have been periods of the season when he failed to perform at his desired level, despite achieving a series of firsts in his career. The 24-year-old contested his first Grand Slam final in September at the US Open, where he was beaten in four sets by Alexander Zverev.

Shelton has also successfully defended his title at the Canadian Masters, as well as winning two ATP 500s and one 250 since January. Earlier this month, he was runner-up at the Paris Masters to Carlos Alcaraz. Shelton’s results secured him a place in the ATP Finals for the first time, where he made it out of the group stages before falling to Alcaraz in the semi-finals on Saturday .
